title: Are You Thinking Character Arc About Now?
use_cases: Use when mapping out a character's transformation from a broken state to being whole
Configure when balancing inner and outer motivations for a protagonist
Implement when integrating external conflict obstacles with internal yearningss
Use when following a blueprint for the most common story arc structure
content:
You’re bang on! This scenario, taking a character from broken to whole, is known as the Change Arc. This is the most common type of arc and is all about transformation and growth. Full of ups and downs, it can be difficult to write, so let me share a blueprint to help.

(I’m including hyperlinks for all the big working pieces, so if you haven’t read The Emotional Wound Thesaurus, they can help to show how everything fits.)

At the start of a story, the character is seeking to obtain her goal (outer motivation), which she may be pursuing to either avoid something undesirable or to satisfy a yearning (inner motivation). The pursuit of this objective is difficult or may seems impossible. There might be roadblocks in the way and people or forces standing against the character (outer conflict), but the unmet need continues to drive her toward her goal.
